albums.blurb: Francisco Tenório Jr. was the pianist of Rio de Janeiro's Beco das Garrafas scene, the nightclub alley where samba-jazz took shape in the early 1960s. Embalo, cut for the RGE label in February and March 1964 with a band including Paulo Moura on alto sax, J.T. Meirelles on tenor and Milton Banana on drums, mixes hard-swinging originals with instrumental readings of bossa nova standards like Jobim's "Inútil Paisagem" and Baden Powell's "Consolação." It was the only album he released in his lifetime: he worked as a sideman for Elis Regina, Edu Lobo and Vinicius de Moraes until March 1976, when he disappeared in Buenos Aires during a tour, an early victim of Argentina's military repression — the story told in Fernando Trueba and Javier Mariscal's 2023 animated documentary They Shot the Piano Player.
albums.reception: Embalo is regarded as a landmark of Brazilian samba-jazz, and decades of collector demand for the scarce original LP led to reissues, including one by the UK label Mr Bongo in 2017.

albums.blurb: Yebba is Abbey Smith from West Memphis, Arkansas, who broke out with a viral 2016 Sofar Sounds performance of "My Mind" and guest turns with Sam Smith, Chance the Rapper and Mark Ronson. Dawn, her debut album, released on RCA in September 2021 and named for her late mother, was produced mainly with Ronson in a run of sessions at Electric Lady Studios; it ranges across 1970s-styled soul, gospel and hip-hop, with Smino, A$AP Rocky and Questlove among the contributors.
albums.reception: Dawn holds a Metacritic score of 84 out of 100 and earned a nomination for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical at the 2022 Grammy Awards.

albums.blurb: Talk Talk started as a London synth-pop band, but by their fourth album singer Mark Hollis had abandoned pop structure altogether. Spirit of Eden, released on Parlophone in 1988, was distilled from months of largely improvised sessions at Wessex Studios — recorded with a rotating cast of jazz, classical and choral musicians, often playing in near darkness — into six slow, quiet pieces that fuse rock, jazz, ambient and chamber music. The band declined to tour it, and together with its 1991 successor Laughing Stock it became the template cited for the post-rock movement.
albums.reception: Spirit of Eden peaked at number 19 on the UK Albums Chart, and it has since been widely credited with pioneering post-rock.
